question: If \[ f\left(\frac{x}{x-1}\right)=\frac1x \] for all \(x\notin\{0,1\},\) and \(0\lt\theta\lt\frac{\pi}{2},\) then \(f(\sec^2\theta)=\)
solution:
To evaluate \(f\) at the requested number, choose \(x\) so that the fraction inside \(f\) equals that number. Set \(t=\sec^2\theta\). Because \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), we have \(0<\cos^2\theta<1\), so \(t>1\).

Solving \(x/(x-1)=t\) gives
\[
x=t(x-1),\qquad (t-1)x=t,
\]
and hence
\[
x=\frac{t}{t-1}.
\]
This value is greater than \(1\), so it avoids both excluded values \(0\) and \(1\). The supplied identity therefore applies and gives
\[
f(t)=\frac1x=\frac{t-1}{t}.
\]
Substituting \(t=\sec^2\theta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(\sec^2\theta)
&=1-\frac1{\sec^2\theta}\\
&=1-\cos^2\theta\\
&=\boxed{\sin^2\theta}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The identity \(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1\) suggests an input whose subtraction by \(1\) produces a cosine term. Choose
\[
x=\csc^2\theta=\frac1{\sin^2\theta}.
\]
Since \(0<\theta<\pi/2\), both \(\sin^2\theta\) and \(\cos^2\theta\) are positive, and \(0<\sin^2\theta<1\). Thus \(x>1\), so the chosen input is allowed and every denominator below is nonzero.

Now
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{x}{x-1}
&=\frac{1/\sin^2\theta}{(1-\sin^2\theta)/\sin^2\theta}\\
&=\frac1{\cos^2\theta}\\
&=\sec^2\theta.
\end{aligned}
\]
Applying the given rule at this \(x\) immediately yields
\[
f(\sec^2\theta)=\frac1x
=\boxed{\sin^2\theta},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Choose a trigonometric input directly
